# If This Was a Movie

"**If This Was a Movie**" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Taylor Swift. It was originally released on October 25, 2010, as a bonus track on the deluxe edition of her third studio album, *Speak Now* (2010). Swift wrote the song with Martin Johnson, the lead singer of the band Boys Like Girls, and produced it alongside Nathan Chapman. Musically, it is a fast-paced pop rock ballad featuring electric guitars and orchestral elements. Lyrically, the song narrates a plea to a former lover to return, invoking cinematic tropes such as standing in the rain and happy endings to contrast with the reality of a breakup.

The track is notable for being the only song on the standard or deluxe editions of *Speak Now* that was not written solely by Swift. Following its digital release as a promotional single on November 8, 2011, "If This Was a Movie" achieved commercial success, debuting at number 10 on the US *Billboard* Hot 100 and number 17 on the Canadian Hot 100. It also charted in the United Kingdom.

In 2023, Swift released a re-recorded version of the song titled "**If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)**". It was released on March 17, 2023, as part of a streaming compilation EP titled *The More Fearless (Taylor's Version) Chapter*. Although originally a *Speak Now* track, the re-recording was grouped with the *Fearless* era to allow the re-recorded version of *Speak Now* to consist entirely of self-written songs. The re-recorded version peaked at number one on the US Country Digital Song Sales chart. Swift performed the song live for the first time in June 2023 during The Eras Tour.

## Background and Release

Taylor Swift wrote her third studio album, *Speak Now* (2010), as a concept album about things she wanted to say to people in her life but never did . While Swift wrote the standard edition of the album entirely by herself, "If This Was a Movie" was co-written with Martin Johnson, the frontman of the American rock band Boys Like Girls . The two had previously collaborated on the song "Two Is Better Than One" by Boys Like Girls and "You'll Always Find Your Way Back Home" from the *Hannah Montana: The Movie* soundtrack .

"If This Was a Movie" was included as the sixteenth track on the deluxe edition of *Speak Now*, which was released exclusively through Target stores in the United States on October 25, 2010 . On November 8, 2011, Big Machine Records released the song, along with other bonus tracks from the album, to digital retailers such as iTunes and Amazon as a promotional single .

## Composition and Lyrics

"If This Was a Movie" is a pop rock ballad characterized by a fast tempo . The production incorporates a recurring guitar riff, acoustic and electric string instruments, drums, and full orchestration . Critics have noted the song's "simple harmonies" in the chorus which support Swift's vocals .

Lyrically, the song deals with the aftermath of a breakup. The narrator daydreams about a lost love returning and wishes that real life would mimic the plot of a romantic movie . The lyrics reference common cinematic tropes, including a lover waiting outside in the rain and a flashback to happier times . In the chorus, Swift sings: "Come back, come back, come back to me like you would, you would if this was a movie / Stand in the rain outside 'til I came out" .

The song's title and lyrical content have drawn comparisons to other tracks in Swift's discography. The chorus parallels the *Fearless* track "Breathe," which mentions music playing "like the end of a sad movie," and the *Fearless (Taylor's Version)* vault track "Bye Bye Baby," which contains the line "It wasn't just like a movie" . The song's title uses the subjunctive mood "was" rather than the grammatically traditional "were" (i.e., "If This Were a Movie"), a usage that is common in modern informal English and appears in other popular songs such as Beyoncé's "If I Were a Boy" and Miranda Lambert's "If I Was a Cowboy" .

## Critical Reception

Upon its release as a promotional single, "If This Was a Movie" received generally positive reviews. *Billboard* rated the track four out of five stars, stating that it showcased a "more age-appropriate track" for Swift and noted that she was examining "more mature content" by departing from high school fantasy themes .

Retrospective rankings of Swift's discography have placed the song in varying positions. In a 2020 ranking of Swift's songs, *Paste* magazine placed the track at number 115 out of 158, with the reviewer criticizing the phrasing of the line "Come back to me like" . *NME* ranked the song 150th out of 161 tracks in 2020, describing it as "frustratingly repetitive" and stating that it "stutters towards the finish line" . In 2025, Rob Sheffield of *Rolling Stone* ranked the song 266th out of 286 songs .

## Commercial Performance

Following its digital release in November 2011, "If This Was a Movie" debuted at number 10 on the US *Billboard* Hot 100 . This achievement made it the fourth track from the *Speak Now* era to reach the top ten and extended Swift's record at the time for the most top-ten debuts by any artist . The song also reached number three on the US Digital Songs chart, selling approximately 163,000 downloads in its first week . Additionally, it peaked at number one on the US Country Digital Song Sales chart .

Internationally, the song charted at number 17 on the Canadian Hot 100 and number 10 on the Canadian Digital Song Sales chart . In the United Kingdom, the song reached number 191 on the UK Singles Chart .

## Live Performances

Swift did not perform "If This Was a Movie" live during the Speak Now World Tour (2011–2012) . The song made its live debut nearly 13 years after its release during The Eras Tour. Swift performed the song on piano as a "surprise song" during her concert in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on June 23, 2023 . Prior to this performance, it was the only song from the *Speak Now* era that had never been performed live .

## If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)

A re-recorded version of the song, titled "**If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)**", was released on March 17, 2023 . It was released alongside re-recordings of "Safe & Sound" and "Eyes Open," as well as the previously unreleased track "All of the Girls You Loved Before," in celebration of the commencement of The Eras Tour .

Although the original song was a track on *Speak Now*, the re-recording was not included on the 2023 re-recorded album *Speak Now (Taylor's Version)*. Instead, it was released as a standalone single and included on a streaming compilation EP titled *The More Fearless (Taylor's Version) Chapter* . The artwork for the single utilizes the cover art from *Fearless (Taylor's Version)* .

Media outlets and fans noted that this shift in "era" assignment—moving the track from *Speak Now* to *Fearless*—was likely due to Swift's intention for *Speak Now (Taylor's Version)* to be an entirely self-written album . Because "If This Was a Movie" was co-written with Martin Johnson, its inclusion would have prevented the re-recorded album from having solely Swift's writing credits . Consequently, "If This Was a Movie" is the only song in Swift's catalog to change its associated era during her re-recording project .

### Production and Reception
"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" was produced by Swift and Christopher Rowe . The re-recording features the same lyrical content and composition as the original. Critics noted Swift's vocals on the re-recording had improved, with *The Times* describing it as "straightforward, innocent, slightly breathy balladry with an orchestral backing" .

Commercially, the re-recorded version reached number two on the US Bubbling Under Hot 100 chart and number four on the US Digital Songs chart . It also became Swift's 19th number-one entry on the US Country Digital Song Sales chart, making "If This Was a Movie" the first song to top that specific chart with two different versions . In New Zealand, the song entered the Hot 40 Singles chart at number 12 .

## Credits and Personnel

**Original Version (2010)**
* **Taylor Swift** – songwriter, producer 
* **Martin Johnson** – songwriter 
* **Nathan Chapman** – producer 

**Taylor's Version (2023)**
* **Taylor Swift** – vocals, songwriter, producer 
* **Martin Johnson** – songwriter 
* **Christopher Rowe** – producer, vocal engineer 
* **David Payne** – recording engineer 
* **Serban Ghenea** – mixer 
* **Randy Merrill** – mastering engineer 
* **Matt Billingslea** – drums 
* **Paul Sidoti** – electric guitar 
* **Mike Meadows** – acoustic guitar, background vocals

#### Songfacts®:

*   This bonus track from the Deluxe edition of Taylor Swift's third studio album **Speak Now** was released as a promotional single for digital download to iTunes and Amazon on November 8, 2011. Taylor wrote the song with Martin Johnson, who is lead singer of Boys Like Girls. Previous collaborations between the pair include "[You'll Always Find Your Way Back Home](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/hannah-montana/youll-always-find-your-way-back-home) " from the soundtrack of _Hannah Montana: The Movie_ and the Boys Like Girls single "[Two Is Better Than One](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/boys-like-girls/two-is-better-than-one)."
    
*   Here, Taylor Swift daydreams of her lost love's return, just like they do in romantic movies. The lyrics reference many classic movie tropes, such as Swift's lover waiting in the rain for her, a flashback to carefree times together, and a happy ending.
    
*   _You would, you would if this was a movie  
    Stand in the rain outside 'til I came out_  
      
    The chorus parallels Swift's 2008 **Fearless** track "[Breathe](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/taylor-swift/breathe)" where she sings:  
      
    _Music starts playin' like the end of a sad movie,  
    It's the kinda ending you don't really wanna see_  
      
    And also Swift's 2021 **Fearless (Taylor's Version)** cut, "[Bye Bye Baby](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/taylor-swift/bye-bye-baby)":  
      
    _It wasn't just like a movie  
    The rain didn't soak through my clothes, down to my skin  
    I'm drivin' away and I, I guess you could say_
    
*   Some grammar pedants complained about the title, believing Swift should have named the song "If This _Were_ A Movie." In traditional grammar, the use of "were" in the subjunctive mood is the correct form to use when expressing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition, but in modern usage, "was" is often used in informal settings instead of "were," and is generally acceptable. We're assuming Swift knew this, since she was a straight-A student.  
      
    The more formal "were" shows up in songs like "[If I Were A Carpenter](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/bobby-darin/if-i-were-a-carpenter)" and "[If I Were Your Woman](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/gladys-knight-the-pips/if-i-were-your-woman)" that carry some gravity. Beyoncé, too, on "[If I Were a Boy](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/beyonce/if-i-were-a-boy)." The "was" form can be heard on "[If I Was a Folkstar](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/the-avalanches/if-i-was-a-folkstar)" by The Avalanches, "[If I Was A Cowboy](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/miranda-lambert/if-i-was-a-cowboy)" by Miranda Lambert, and "[If I Was Your Girlfriend](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/prince/if-i-was-your-girlfriend)" by Prince, who seemed to transcend the rules of grammar.
    
*   "If This Was A Movie" was the only song on the deluxe edition of **Speak Now** to feature a co-writer.

#### [Twilight Zone](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/golden-earring/twilight-zone)Golden Earring

"Twilight Zone" by Golden Earring was inspired by the Robert Ludlum novel The Bourne Identity, not by the TV show.

[![Image 9: The Pussycat Dolls](https://www.songfacts.com/img-artalbums-240-78f39a04ea8b71d5d159ad64c668b367.png)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/the-pussycat-dolls/dont-cha)

#### [Don't Cha](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/the-pussycat-dolls/dont-cha)The Pussycat Dolls

Sir Mix-A-Lot is credited as a writer on The Pussycat Dolls' biggest hit, "Don't Cha," because it interpolates his 1988 song "Swass," where he goes, "Don't you wish your boyfriend was swass like me?"

[![Image 10: Eagles](https://www.songfacts.com/img-artalbums-240-4b2f6c1911c8a36bdf712e59dc7a9607.png)](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/eagles/hotel-california)

#### [Hotel California](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/eagles/hotel-california)Eagles

Many people believe "Hotel California" is about a mental institution called the Camarillo, but the Eagles say it's about materialism and excess.

### Editor's Picks

[![Image 11: Devo](https://www.songfacts.com/img-blog-240-86.jpg)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/devo)

#### [Devo](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/devo)Songwriter Interviews

Devo founders Mark Mothersbaugh and Jerry Casale take us into their world of subversive performance art. They may be right about the De-Evoloution thing.

[![Image 12: Church Lyrics](https://www.songfacts.com/img-blog-240-772.jpg)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/quiz/church-lyrics)

#### [Church Lyrics](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/quiz/church-lyrics)Music Quiz

Here is the church, here is the steeple - see if you can identify these lyrics that reference church.

[![Image 13: Lajon Witherspoon of Sevendust](https://www.songfacts.com/img-blog-240-527.jpg)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/lajon-witherspoon-of-sevendust)

#### [Lajon Witherspoon of Sevendust](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/lajon-witherspoon-of-sevendust)Songwriter Interviews

The Sevendust frontman talks about the group's songwriting process, and how trips to the Murder Bar helped forge their latest album.

[![Image 14: Timothy B. Schmit](https://www.songfacts.com/img-blog-240-1039.jpg)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/timothy-b-schmit)

#### [Timothy B. Schmit](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/timothy-b-schmit)Songwriter Interviews

The longtime Eagle talks about soaring back to his solo career, and what he learned about songwriting in the group.

[![Image 15: Donnie Iris (Ah! Leah!, The Rapper)](https://www.songfacts.com/img-blog-240-75.jpg)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/donnie-iris-ah-leah-the-rapper)

#### [Donnie Iris (Ah! Leah!, The Rapper)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/donnie-iris-ah-leah-the-rapper)Songwriter Interviews

Before "Rap" was a form of music, it was something guys did to pick up girls in nightclubs. Donnie talks about "The Rapper" and reveals the identity of Leah.

[![Image 16: Philip Cody](https://www.songfacts.com/img-blog-240-230.jpg)](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/philip-cody)

#### [Philip Cody](https://www.songfacts.com/blog/interviews/philip-cody)Songwriter Interviews

A talented lyricist, Philip helped revive Neil Sedaka's career with the words to "Laughter In The Rain" and "Bad Blood."

[countdown](https://countrycountdownusa.com/author/countdown/ "Posts by countdown") | November 16, 2011

“60 MINUTES” PROFILE OF TAYLOR SWIFT TO AIR SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 20TH AT 7 PM ET / PT ON CBS

TAYLOR CELEBRATES 4TH CONSECUTIVE #1 SINGLE, THREE NEW BILLBOARD HOT 100 DEBUTS

NASHVILLE – November 16, 2011 – Four-time Grammy winner and Billboard’s 2011 Woman of the Year Taylor Swift will be profiled this Sunday, November 20th, on CBS News’ 60 Minutes. The segment includes concert and backstage footage from Taylor’s blockbuster Speak Now World Tour, and correspondent Lesley Stahl’s in-depth report offers viewers a candid conversation with Taylor, as well as a first-ever glimpse inside her Nashville condominium.  The full profile will be posted online at www.60minutes.com immediately after the show airs.

This week alone, Taylor sold more than 545,000 digital tracks. She debuted three new tracks (songs previously only available on the Target Deluxe Edition of Speak Now) on the all-genre Billboard Hot 100 singles chart, with “If This Was A Movie,” “Ours,” and “Superman,” entering the chart at numbers 10, 13 and 26, respectively. “Movie” marks Taylor’s Hot 100-record-extending eighth title to debut in the Top 10. She also locked down three of iTunes’ all-genre Top 10 spots, including positions #1 and #2, the day after the songs’ release.

Also this week, Taylor, who just last week was crowned Entertainer of the Year by the Country Music Association (for the second time), reached the #1 spot atop both the Billboard and Country Aircheck/Mediabase Country radio charts, with “Sparks Fly” becoming Taylor’s 4th consecutive #1 single from her 5 million plus-selling Speak Now album, and her 9th #1 song.

The 60 Minutes profile comes on the eve of the November 21st Big Machine Records release of SPEAK NOW WORLD TOUR – LIVE, CD / DVD combo-pak sets of the show. The North American leg of the tour wraps with sold-out shows at Madison Square Garden on November 21st and 22nd, and the tour has been extended into 2012 with shows in Australia and New Zealand.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

| "If This Was a Movie" |

| [Promotional single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promotional_single "Promotional single") by [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") |
| from the album _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now "Speak Now")_ |
| Released | November 8, 2011 |
| [Genre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_genre "Music genre") | 
*   [Pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock")

 |

| [Label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_label "Record label") | [Big Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records") |
| [Songwriters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriter "Songwriter") |

 |
| [Producers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_producer "Record producer") |

*   [Nathan Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Chapman_/(record_producer/) "Nathan Chapman (record producer)")

 |
|  |
| Official audio |
| ["If This Was a Movie"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ddEDXz9hRP4) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_/(identifier/) "YouTube video (identifier)") |

"**If This Was a Movie**" is a song by the American singer-songwriter [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") from the deluxe edition of her third studio album _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now "Speak Now")_ (2010). She wrote the track with [Martin Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Johnson_/(musician/) "Martin Johnson (musician)") and produced it with [Nathan Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Chapman_/(record_producer/) "Nathan Chapman (record producer)"). A fast-paced [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad"), "If This Was a Movie" includes both acoustic and electric [string instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument"), drums, [key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_instrument "Keyboard instrument") notes, and full [orchestration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchestration "Orchestration"). In the lyrics, Swift's character begs an ex-lover to return to her and expects him to do so like it was a movie.

[Big Machine Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records") released "If This Was a Movie" digitally through the [iTunes Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Store "ITunes Store") on November 8, 2011. The song reached charts in Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States, where it debuted within the top ten of the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). Two publication reviews of the track were published in late 2011; one found it engaging, and the other deemed that it showcased newfound maturity within Swift's lyrics. Retrospective rankings of [Swift's songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_songs_by_Taylor_Swift "List of songs by Taylor Swift") have included the track within the lower-tier positions.

On March 17, 2023, Swift released a [re-recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-recording_/(music/) "Re-recording (music)") of the song, titled "**If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)**", alongside three other songs to [streaming services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") in celebration of the start of her [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), where she debuted it live on piano during a [Minneapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneapolis "Minneapolis") show on June 23. The re-recording was also part of an effort to re-record her early catalog after a [dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_masters_dispute "Taylor Swift masters dispute") over the ownership of the [master recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_recordings "Master recordings").

Background and release
----------------------

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=If_This_Was_a_Movie&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and release")\]

[![Image 2: Martin Johnson wearing a black outfit with an electric guitar smiling](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c4/Martin-Johnson_blg.jpg/250px-Martin-Johnson_blg.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Martin-Johnson_blg.jpg)

[Martin Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Johnson_/(musician/) "Martin Johnson (musician)") co-wrote "If This Was a Movie".

[Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") conceived her third studio album, _[Speak Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now "Speak Now")_ (2010), as a collection of tracks about the things she had wanted to say but was unable to do with the people she had met.[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Conger-1) There were as many as 25 songs Swift wrote for the album,[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Conger-1) which she co-produced with [Nathan Chapman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Chapman_/(record_producer/) "Nathan Chapman (record producer)"),[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Pastorek-2010-2) who had worked on her previous releases.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-3) By around mid-2010, she had secured the final track list,[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-4) where all the tracks were written by her.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Pastorek-2010-2) One exception, however, was "If This Was a Movie", which Swift wrote with [Martin Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Johnson_/(musician/) "Martin Johnson (musician)") alongside other songs.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski202471-5)

"If This Was a Movie" was included as a [bonus track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonus_track "Bonus track") in _Speak Now_'s deluxe edition,[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-6) which was released as a [Target](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_Corporation "Target Corporation")\-exclusive alongside the standard edition on October 25, 2010.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-7) [Big Machine Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Machine_Records "Big Machine Records") made the song digitally available, along with the other bonus tracks, through the [iTunes Store](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes_Store "ITunes Store") on November 8, 2011.[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTESpencer2013106-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-9) On June 23, 2023, Swift debuted the track live on piano during a show in [Minneapolis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneapolis "Minneapolis"), as part of her [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour") (2023–2024).[\[10\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-10)

Produced by Swift and Chapman,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Billboard-2011-11) "If This Was a Movie" is a [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock") [ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") that critics described as "somber" and "sparkling".[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski202471-5)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Lane-2023-12) Set on a fast pace,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Billboard-2011-11) it has a length of 5 minutes and 48 seconds.[\[13\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-13) According to the _[Seattle Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seattle_Weekly "Seattle Weekly")_'s Erin Thompson, the song has a basic arrangement and structure, which he regarded as "[Swiftian](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Swiftian "wikt:Swiftian")".[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Thompson-2011-14) It features acoustic [string instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/String_instrument "String instrument") from [country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") and [folk music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music"), an electric guitar [amplified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar_amplifier "Guitar amplifier") by [distortion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distortion_/(music/) "Distortion (music)"), and full [orchestration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchestration "Orchestration").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201741-15) The [musicologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musicologist "Musicologist") James E. Perone said that this arrangement could give "mixed-genre messages" to listeners.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201741-15) A simple, recurring guitar [riff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riff "Riff") is also played throughout,[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Billboard-2011-11) while drums and [key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_instrument "Keyboard instrument") notes lead Swift.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Thompson-2011-14) The [verse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verse_/(music/) "Verse (music)")'s melody is performed at a low [register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vocal_register "Vocal register") and built on short [motive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motif_/(music/) "Motif (music)") [figures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Figure_/(music/) "Figure (music)").[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201741-15) The dramatic [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain"),[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski202471-5) where Swift sings with a [twang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twang "Twang") accompanied by [harmonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmony "Harmony"),[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Billboard-2011-11) [contrasts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contrast_/(music/) "Contrast (music)") the verse by being more melodious and performed at a higher register.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201741-15)

In the lyrics, Swift's character pleads an ex-lover, who had left for six months, to come back to her, expecting him to do as such like it was a movie.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski202471-5)[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-:1-16) She imagines that through this perspective, he would be sorry to her for what mistake he made, and she would accept his apology and reconcile with him.[\[15\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPerone201741-15) A staff from _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")_ said that she was in a state of [coming of age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_of_age "Coming of age") in the lyrics, believing that she departs from the "fantasy world of high school" and examines "more mature content".[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Billboard-2011-11) Swift on the song often recalls the important memories when they were together.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski202471-5) It also includes a lyric about being in the rain ("Stand in the rain/'Til I came out"), which Thompson felt was used extensively in her songs.[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-17)[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Thompson-2011-14) By the conclusion, the ideal ending does not happen like Swift had hoped for.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZaleski202471-5)

In late 2011, two publication reviews of "If This Was a Movie" were issued. Thompson included it in the _Seattle Weekly_'s "Nice Hits!"—a [column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Column_/(periodical/) "Column (periodical)") that explores the best tracks out of the [top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_40 "Top 40") songs in a given time. He believed that while not "lyrically perfect", the track had the features that made Swift's songs engaging, including for what he considered vulnerable, relatable songwriting and a simple composition.[\[14\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Thompson-2011-14) _Billboard_'s staff stated that it showcased "a more age-appropriate track" from her.[\[11\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Billboard-2011-11)

Over the years, retrospective rankings of [Swift's songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_songs_by_Taylor_Swift "List of songs by Taylor Swift") have included "If This Was a Movie" within the lower-tier positions. _[Paste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_/(magazine/) "Paste (magazine)")_'s ranking, published in February 2020, listed the track as 115th among her 158 songs—one of its writers Jane Song took issue with the line, "Come back to me like", which she heard as "Come back to me, daylight".[\[17\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-18) In her September 2020 ranking of Swift's 161 tracks for _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_, Hannah Mylrea placed the song at 150th, writing that "it stutters towards the finish line" and that it was "frustratingly repetitive" overall.[\[18\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-19) [Rob Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Sheffield "Rob Sheffield") listed the track as 266th in his October 2025 ranking of her 286 songs for _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_.[\[19\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-20) The next month, Nate Jones of _[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_/(website/) "Vulture (website)")_ updated his ranking of Swift's 245 tracks, where the song was placed at 170th; he viewed it as "the [mirror image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirror_image "Mirror image")" of her track "[White Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Horse_/(Taylor_Swift_song/) "White Horse (Taylor Swift song)")" (2008) that, to him, made it "oddly superfluous".[\[20\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-21)

Carena Liptak of _[Taste of Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taste_of_Country "Taste of Country")_ included the song as 16th in her 2023 ranking of all 17 original tracks from _Speak Now_'s deluxe edition, saying that the song, while not among the album's most memorable, displayed "Swift's heartbreak songwriting at its wistful, [earworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earworm "Earworm")\-y best" and that its emotional impact was skillfully handled. She attributed the placement to how other tracks better showcase Swift's "ability to wax poetic on heartbreak and nostalgia".[\[21\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-22)

After its digital release in November 2011, "If This Was a Movie" debuted at number ten on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart in the United States, where the track also reached number three on [Digital Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Song_Sales "Digital Song Sales") with 163,000 [downloads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download").[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Trust-2011-23) The top-ten entry on the Hot 100 made the song become the fourth track from _Speak Now_ to do so, in addition to extending Swift's record of most top-ten debuts for any act with ten.[\[22\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Trust-2011-23) It peaked atop on [Country Digital Song Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Digital_Song_Sales "Country Digital Song Sales") as well.[\[23\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-USCDSS-24) Elsewhere, the song reached number 191 in the United Kingdom[\[24\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-UK-25) and number 17 in Canada,[\[25\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-CanadaHot100-26) where it also peaked at number 10 on Canada Digital Song Sales.[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-CanadaDSS-27)

### Release and production

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=If_This_Was_a_Movie&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Release and production")\]

To celebrate the start of the Eras Tour on March 17, 2023, Swift released a [re-recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Re-recording_/(music/) "Re-recording (music)") of the song, titled "If This Was a Movie" (Taylor's Version)", on that day alongside three other songs to [streaming services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media").[\[29\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-30)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Aguja-2023-31) The re-recording was also part of an attempt to re-record her early catalog after a [dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift_masters_dispute "Taylor Swift masters dispute") over the ownership of the [master recordings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_recordings "Master recordings").[\[31\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-32) It has the same cover art as that of Swift's re-recorded album, _[Fearless (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fearless_/(Taylor%27s_Version/) "Fearless (Taylor's Version)")_ (2021), and was included on the [compilation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"), _The More Fearless (Taylor's Version) Chapter_,[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Aguja-2023-31) which was also released on that day.[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-:2-33) Speculation ensued amongst fans regarding the song's release, according to some journalists, who questioned whether it would be featured on _Speak Now_'s re-recording, _[Speak Now (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speak_Now_/(Taylor%27s_Version/) "Speak Now (Taylor's Version)")_ (2023).[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-35)[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Aguja-2023-31)[\[12\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Lane-2023-12) When the album's track list was unveiled on June 5, 2023, the song was not on it.[\[33\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Sager-2023-34)

"If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" has a length of 3 minutes and 57 seconds.[\[34\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-36) _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times "The Times")_'s [Will Hodgkinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Hodgkinson "Will Hodgkinson") described it as "straightforward, innocent, slightly breathy balladry with an orchestral backing".[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-:1-16) The song was produced by Swift and its vocal engineer [Christopher Rowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Rowe_/(record_producer/) "Christopher Rowe (record producer)"). Musicians on the track were Amos Heller (who played bass), David Cook (piano), Matt Billingslea (drums and percussion), Max Bernstein (electric guitar), Mike Meadows (acoustic guitar), and Paul Sidoti (electric guitar); Bernstein also provided synthesizer [programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_/(music/) "Programming (music)"), while Meadows was the background vocalist. The [engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_engineer "Audio engineer") were Bryce Bordone and Derek Garten, who was also the editor alongside Lowell Reynolds. David Payne was the recording engineer, assisted by Reynolds. The [mixer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mixing_engineer "Mixing engineer") was [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea"), while the [mastering engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastering_engineer "Mastering engineer") was [Randy Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Merrill "Randy Merrill").[\[32\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-:2-33)

### Critical reception and chart performance

\[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=If_This_Was_a_Movie&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Critical reception and chart performance")\]

In two reviews of the four songs that were released right before the start of Swift's Eras Tour, "If This Was a Movie" (Taylor's Version)" received favorable comments. Writing for _[The Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Freeman_/(newspaper/) "The Freeman (newspaper)")_, Januar Junior Aguja said that the track could have new fans because of Swift's vocals on the re-recording, claiming that they had improved.[\[30\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Aguja-2023-31) Hodgkinson wrote that the song was "corny but smart" and, to him, had Swift's early brilliance of "capturing an entire romantic drama in three minutes", considering that it had both an "[ingenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ing%C3%A9nue "Ingénue") spirit" and professionally-written ruthlessness.[\[16\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-:1-16)

Commercially, "If This Was a Movie (Taylor's Version)" reached number two on the [Bubbling Under Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubbling_Under_Hot_100 "Bubbling Under Hot 100")[\[35\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-USBUH100-37) and number four on Digital Songs in the US with 11,300 downloads.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Trust-2023-38) On Country Digital Song Sales, it became her record-extending 19th number-one entry and made "If This Was a Movie" the first song to have two versions peak atop the chart.[\[36\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-Trust-2023-38) On sales-component charts in other countries, the song reached number seven on Canada Digital Song Sales[\[26\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-CanadaDSS-27) and number thirteen on both [UK Singles Downloads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Downloads_Chart "UK Singles Downloads Chart") and [UK Singles Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Sales_Chart "UK Singles Sales Chart").[\[37\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-UKDownloads-39)[\[38\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-UKSales-40) It also entered at number twelve on [Hot 40 Singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Aotearoa_Music_Charts#Hot_Singles_chart "Official Aotearoa Music Charts") in New Zealand.[\[39\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_This_Was_a_Movie#cite_note-NZH40S-41)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars"), and [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") (_pictured in order_) tied for the most top-ten singles in 2011 with six each. Mars's "[Grenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenade_/(song/) "Grenade (song)")" had a four-week run at number one on the [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100") and ranked number six on [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [year-end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End "Billboard Year-End") [Hot 100 list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2011 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2011"). Rihanna became the fastest solo artist to collect twenty top-ten hits when her single "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" (featuring [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris")) entered the top ten six years and four months after she first appeared on the Hot 100. The song, as well as her single "[S&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%26M_/(song/) "S&M (song)")" (featuring [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears")), climbed to number one on the chart, "S&M" logging one week at the top and "We Found Love" logging ten weeks, including two in 2012. Seventy-one singles made into top 10 of the [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100"), the all-genre _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")_ singles charts, in 2011. Sixty-eight acts had a top-ten hit during the year, with twenty achieving their first either as a lead or featured artist. [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne"), [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars"), and [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") each had six top-ten hits in 2011, tying them for the most top-ten hits during the year. [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO_/(group/) "LMFAO (group)")'s "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" (featuring [Lauren Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauren_Bennett "Lauren Bennett") and [GoonRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoonRock "GoonRock")) had a twenty-six-week run in the top ten, the longest during the year and tying with [Savage Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savage_Garden "Savage Garden")'s "[Truly Madly Deeply](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truly_Madly_Deeply_/(song/) "Truly Madly Deeply (song)")" as the fourth-longest in _Billboard_ history. In the beginning of 2012, the song re-entered the top ten, extending its run to twenty-nine weeks and becoming the fourth-longest-running top-ten single ever behind "[How Do I Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_Do_I_Live "How Do I Live")" by [LeAnn Rimes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeAnn_Rimes "LeAnn Rimes"), "[Smooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_/(Santana_song/) "Smooth (Santana song)")" by [Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santana_/(band/) "Santana (band)") featuring [Rob Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Thomas_/(musician/) "Rob Thomas (musician)") and "[Uptown Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Funk "Uptown Funk")" by [Mark Ronson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Ronson "Mark Ronson") featuring [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars"), also bumping [Jewel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewel_/(singer/) "Jewel (singer)")'s [You Were Meant For Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Were_Meant_for_Me_/(Jewel_song/) "You Were Meant for Me (Jewel song)")/[Foolish Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foolish_Games "Foolish Games") down to fifth, with 28 weeks. On the week ending April 30, 2011, singer [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry") extended her top ten streak beginning the previous year to forty-nine weeks, breaking a record held by Swedish pop band [Ace of Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_of_Base "Ace of Base") for seventeen years. Perry went on to log twenty more consecutive weeks in the top ten, extending her record to sixty-nine weeks, before "[Last Friday Night (T.G.I.F.)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Friday_Night_/(T.G.I.F./) "Last Friday Night (T.G.I.F.)")" fell out of the top ten on the week ending September 24, 2011, ending her streak. Rihanna attained her twentieth top-ten hit when "[We Found Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Found_Love "We Found Love")" (featuring [Calvin Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Harris "Calvin Harris")) climbed into the top ten on the week ending October 15, 2011. This made Rihanna the fastest soloist to attain twenty top-ten hits, having done so in a six-year, four-month span, breaking a record previously held by singer [Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madonna "Madonna"). [![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Wiz_Khalifa_2010.jpg/250px-Wiz_Khalifa_2010.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wiz_Khalifa_2010.jpg) American rapper and singer [Wiz Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiz_Khalifa "Wiz Khalifa") scored two top-ten singles with "[Black and Yellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_and_Yellow "Black and Yellow")". The song became his first number-one hit, and ranked number thirty-one on [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [year-end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End "Billboard Year-End") [Hot 100 list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2011 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2011"). Meanwhile "[No Sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Sleep_/(Wiz_Khalifa_song/) "No Sleep (Wiz Khalifa song)")" which debuted at number 6, would end up being his second top-ten hit . [![Image 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Drake_at_Bun-B_Concert_2011_%281%29.jpg/250px-Drake_at_Bun-B_Concert_2011_%281%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Drake_at_Bun-B_Concert_2011_/(1/).jpg) Canadian rapper and singer [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_/(musician/) "Drake (musician)") scored three top-ten singles with his features on "[What's My Name?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What%27s_My_Name%3F_/(Rihanna_song/) "What's My Name? (Rihanna song)")" with [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") which charted at number 1, [DJ Khaled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJ_Khaled "DJ Khaled")'s "[I'm On One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I%27m_On_One "I'm On One")" with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne") and [Rick Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Ross "Rick Ross") which charted at number 10 and [She Will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Will "She Will") with [Lil Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Wayne "Lil Wayne") which charted at number 3. [![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Katy_Perry_at_the_2011_Logie_Awards.jpg/250px-Katy_Perry_at_the_2011_Logie_Awards.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Katy_Perry_at_the_2011_Logie_Awards.jpg) In 2011, singer [Katy Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Perry "Katy Perry") broke the record for the longest consecutive run in the top ten after logging forty-nine weeks in the tier; later in the year, she went on to extend this record to sixty-nine weeks. Perry scored four top-ten singles during the year, three of which went to number one and two of which, "[Firework](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firework_/(song/) "Firework (song)")" and "[E.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E.T._/(song/) "E.T. (song)")" (featuring [Kanye West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West")), ranked at numbers three and four respectively on [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [year-end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End "Billboard Year-End") [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100") [list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2011 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2011"). [![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Adele_-_Seattle%2C_WA_-_8.12.2011.jpg/250px-Adele_-_Seattle%2C_WA_-_8.12.2011.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Adele_-_Seattle,_WA_-_8.12.2011.jpg) English singer-songwriter [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adele "Adele") achieved her first top-ten single with "[Rolling in the Deep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_in_the_Deep "Rolling in the Deep")", which logged seven weeks at number one and went on to become [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [number-one single of the year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Year-End_number-one_singles_and_albums "List of Billboard Year-End number-one singles and albums"). She later achieved a second top-ten single with "[Someone Like You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Someone_Like_You_/(Adele_song/) "Someone Like You (Adele song)")", which spent five weeks at number one. [![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/LMFAO_-_Live_Walmart_%281%29.jpg/250px-LMFAO_-_Live_Walmart_%281%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LMFAO_-_Live_Walmart_/(1/).jpg) Electropop duo [LMFAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMFAO_/(group/) "LMFAO (group)") had the longest-running top-ten single in 2011 with "[Party Rock Anthem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Rock_Anthem "Party Rock Anthem")" (featuring [Lauren Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lauren_Bennett "Lauren Bennett") and [GoonRock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoonRock "GoonRock")), which remained in the top ten for twenty-six weeks, tying with [Savage Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savage_Garden "Savage Garden")'s "[Truly Madly Deeply](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truly_Madly_Deeply_/(song/) "Truly Madly Deeply (song)")" for the fourth-longest top ten run for a single in [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)") history. In 2012, the song spent three more weeks in the top ten, extending its run to twenty-nine weeks and becoming the third-longest-running top-ten single ever. The song spent six weeks at number one and became _Billboard'_s number-two single of 2011. LMFAO scored a second top-ten single in 2011 with "[Sexy and I Know It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexy_and_I_Know_It "Sexy and I Know It")", which reached number one in 2012. [![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/Maroon_5%2C_2011.jpg/250px-Maroon_5%2C_2011.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Maroon_5,_2011.jpg) Pop rock band [Maroon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroon_5 "Maroon 5") scored their fourth top-ten single with "[Moves Like Jagger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moves_Like_Jagger "Moves Like Jagger")" (featuring [Christina Aguilera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Aguilera "Christina Aguilera")). The song became the band's second number-one hit, remaining at the [Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_100 "Hot 100") summit for four weeks, and ranked number nine on [_Billboard_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_/(magazine/) "Billboard (magazine)")'s [year-end](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End "Billboard Year-End") [Hot 100 list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Year-End_Hot_100_singles_of_2011 "Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2011"). Now (2010) | Fearless (Taylor's Version) \[2021\] Search for: “If This Was A Movie” is track sixteen on the deluxe edition of Taylor’s third studio album, _[Speak Now](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/albums/speak-now-album/)_ (2010). She wishes for a lost love to come back to her, like he would in a movie. The re-recorded version of the song, titled “If This Was A Movie (Taylor’s Version)” was released on March 17, 2023, and is featured on _The More [Fearless (Taylor’s Version)](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/re-recordings/fearless-taylors-version/) Chapter_ EP. ##### Table of Contents ### Background and Lyrical Theme Taylor wrote “If This Was A Movie” with Martin Johnson, who is the lead singer of the band Boys Like Girls. It is her only co-write on _Speak Now_. Previous collaborations between the pair include “[You’ll Always Find Your Way Back Home](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/work-for-other-artists/you-will-always-find-your-way-back-home/)” from the soundtrack of [_Hannah Montana: The Movie_](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/videography/filmography/hannah-montana-the-movie/) and the Boys Like Girls single “[Two Is Better Than One](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/features/two-is-better-than-one/).” A recurring guitar riff moves the song along, while its chorus features simple harmonies providing backup to Taylor’s signature twang. The lyrics suggest that she had gone through a breakup a few months earlier and still hopes things could go back to how they were before: _“I just want it back the way it was before/And I just wanna see you back at my front door.”_ ### Live Performance Taylor first performed “If This Was A Movie” during her sixth headlining concert tour, “[The Eras Tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/tours/taylor-swift-the-eras-tour/)” (2023-2024), almost 13 years after its release. It was the second surprise song during her show on June 23, 2023, in Minneapolis. She performed it acoustically on piano. ### Critical Reception “If This Was A Movie” was released on the deluxe edition of _Speak Now_ and was made a promotional single in November 2011. The song received positive reviews from music critics, with _Billboard_ rating it 4/5 stars. ### Taylor's Version Even though “If This Was A Movie” originally appeared as a deluxe track on _Speak Now,_ the re-recording of the song is featured as a track on the EP _The More Fearless (Taylor’s Version) Chapter_ (2023). It is worth noting that the song was the only track on _Speak Now_ not to be written solely by Taylor. Fans have speculated this might be the reason why it’s now being promoted as a [_Fearless_ _(Taylor’s Version)_](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/re-recordings/fearless-taylors-version/) song. [_Speak Now (Taylor’s Version)_](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.ch/index.php/re-recordings/speak-now-taylors-version/) would be, therefore, entirely written by Taylor alone. ### Lyrics **\[Verse 1\]** Last night I heard my own heart beating Sounded like footsteps on my stairs Six months gone and I’m still reachin’ Even though I know you’re not there I was playing back a thousand memories, baby Thinkin’ ’bout everything we’ve been through Maybe I’ve been going back too much lately When time stood still and I had you **\[Chorus\]** Come back, come back, come back to me Like you would, you would if this was a movie Stand in the rain outside till I came out Come back, come back, come back to me Like you could, you could if you just said you’re sorry I know that we can work it out somehow But if this was a movie you’d be here by now **\[Verse 2\]** I know people change and these things happen But I remember how it was back then Locked up in your arms and our friends are laughing ‘Cause nothing like this ever happened to them Now I’m pacing down the hall, chasing down your street Flashback to a night when you said to me That nothing’s gonna change, not for me and you Not before I knew how much I had to lose **\[Chorus\]** Come back, come back, come back to me Like you would, you would if this was a movie Stand in the rain outside till I came out Come back, come back, come back to me Like you could, you could if you just said you’re sorry I know that we can work it out somehow But if this was a movie you’d be here by now **\[Bridge\]** If you’re out there, if you’re somewhere, if you’re moving on I’ve been waiting for you every day since you’ve been gone I just want it back the way it was before And I just wanna see you back at my front door And I’d say **\[Chorus Variation\]** Come back, come back, come back to me Like you would before you said, “It’s not that easy” Before the fight, before I locked you out But I’d take it all back now **\[Final Chorus\]** Come back, come back, come back to me Like you would, you would if this was a movie Stand in the rain outside till I came out Come back, come back, come back to me Like you could, you could if you just said you’re sorry I know that we could work it out somehow But if this was a movie you’d be here by now **\[Outro\]** You’d be here by now It’s not the kind of ending you wanna see now Baby, what about the ending? Chart Buzz: Drake, Justin Bieber, Mac Miller, Rihanna
=====================================================

[0](https://hifimagazine.net/blog/?p=4826#respond)

Posted November 17, 2011 by [J Matthew Cobb](http://www.hifimagazine.net/jmatthewcobb "Visit J Matthew Cobb’s website") in [News](https://hifimagazine.net/blog/?cat=3)

[![Image 4: chartbuzz-nov16-news-header](https://hifimagazine.net/blog/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/chartbuzz-nov16-news-header.jpg)](https://hifimagazine.net/blog/wp-content/uploads/2011/11/chartbuzz-nov16-news-header.jpg)

In the latest CHART BUZZ, we reveal Justin Bieber, Mac Miller and Drake all sharing the No. 1 slots on the Billboard 200 within the course of three weeks; Rihanna seems to be burning up the Hot 100
=====================================================================================================================================================================================================

Before we speak about next week’s No. 1 on the Billboard 200, let’s talk about last week’s contender first.

**Justin Bieber**‘s holiday effort, _Under The Mistletoe_, shot to No. 1 on its first week of release, selling 210,000 copies. It’s a relatively small number of units sold for the young champ, since he has previously scored two No. 1 albums with _My World 2.0_ and _Never Say Never: The Remixes_.

The album, which features collaborations with Mariah Carey, Busta Rhymes, Usher, The Band Perry and Boyz II Men, also broke the record for being the [first holiday album by a male artist](http://news.yahoo.com/justin-biebers-mistletoe-debuts-no-1-131932335.html) to debut at the top position in the history of the Billboard 200 chart, according to Billboard.com.

Last week, a pile of newer releases dominated the upper tier of the Billboard 200, but revealed signs of even bigger changes in the weeks to come. For instance, **Coldplay**‘s _Mylo Xyloto_ dropped 1-7, while **Florence + the Machine**‘s _Ceremonials_, already in its fourth week on the charts, held tight to No. 6 after dropping from No. 4. **Michael Bublé**‘s _Christmas_ held steady to No. 8, with **Tyrese**‘s _Open Invitation_ remaining strong at No. 9. **Kelly Clarkson**‘s _Stronger_, her fifth studio project, fell 2-10 on its second week of release.

This week, indie rapper **Mac Miller** replaces the Bieb at No. 1 with his debut album _Blue Slide Park_, selling 144,000 copies. The album, released independently with distribution from Fontana becomes the [first indie album to top the chart since 1995](http://www.hitfix.com/articles/indie-underdog-mac-miller-replaces-justin-bieber-at-no-1-on-billboard-200). Big news for Canadian crooner Michael Bublé with his _Christmas_ set; the album soars from 8-2 (123,000 copies sold), while the latest installment in the _NOW! That’s What I Call Music_ compilation series, _Now 40_, made its debut at No. 3, selling 119,000 copies. The soundtrack to Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn enters at No. 4 (105,000), while **Adele** holds to No. 5 with her best-selling _21_ (104,000).

Next week’s Number 1 will definitely be **Drake**. According to [Aceshowbiz](http://www.aceshowbiz.com/news/view/00045357.html), the superstar rapper is expected to take the top spot with his second full-length studio LP _Take Care_, selling well over 700,000 copies. If these reports are true, Drake will become [2011’s third best-seller act based on first-week sales](http://www.billboard.com/news/drake-s-take-care-cruising-to-700-000-plus-1005538192.story#/news/drake-s-take-care-cruising-to-700-000-plus-1005538192.story), with Lady Gaga and Lil Wayne leading the list. Drake’s last album, _Thank Me Later_, scored the No. 1 spot in 2010 with 447,000 copies sold on its first week.

**Rihanna**‘s “We Found Love,” containing a mix from **Calvin Harris**, spends its [third week at No. 1](http://www.billboard.com/news/drake-s-take-care-cruising-to-700-000-plus-1005538192.story#/news/rihanna-still-atop-hot-100-taylor-swift-1005531152.story) on the Billboard Hot 100. “Found,” the lead single from Rihanna’s sixth studio album, _Talk That Talk_, due for release Nov. 21, also spends a third week at No. 1 on the Digital Songs chart with 227,000 downloads sold, down 4%, according to Nielsen SoundScan. On Radio Songs, the dance track lifts 4-3 with 115 million all-format audience impressions, up 12%, according to Nielsen BDS. **Taylor Swift**‘s latst single, “If This Was A Movie,” makes its debut at No. 10. On the Digital Songs’ survey, the song starts at No. 3 with 162,000 downloads sold.

7.content:
Edit here your fullwidth image

![Image 1: "Speak Now" Prologue (Taylor Swift, 2010)](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=361x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/ie87c76cbea1da317/version/1549742566/speak-now-prologue-taylor-swift-2010.jpg)

**"Speak now or forever hold your peace", the words said by the preachers at the end of wedding ceremonies all over the world, right before the vows. It's a last chance for protest, a moment that makes everyone's heart race, and a moment I've always been strangely fascinated by. So many fantasize about bursting into a church, saying what they'd kept inside for years like in the movies. In real life, it rarely happens.**

Real life is a funny thing, you know. In real life, saying the right thing at the right moment is beyond crucial. So crucial, in fact, that most of us start to hesitate, for fear of saying the wrong thing at the wrong time. But lately what I've begun to fear more than that is letting that moment pass without saying anything. I think most of us fear reaching the end of our life, and looking back regretting the moments we didn't speak up. When we didn't say **"I love you"**. When we should've said **"I'm sorry"**. When we didn't stand up for ourselves or someone who needed help.

These songs are made up of words I didn't say when the moment was right in front of me. **These songs are open letters.** Each is written with a specific person in mind, telling them what I meant to tell them in person. To the beautiful boy whose heart I broke in December. To my first love who I never thought would be my first heartbreak. To my band. To a mean man I used to be afraid of. To someone who made my world dark for a while. To a girl who stole something of mine. To someone I forgive for what he said in front of the whole world.

Words can break someone into a million pieces, but they can also put them back together. I hope you use yours for good, because the only words you'll regret more than the ones left unsaid are the ones that you use to intentionally hurt someone. What you say might be too much for some people. Maybe it will come out all wrong and you'll stutter and you'll walk away embarrassed, wincing as you play it all back in your head. But I think the words you stop yourself from saying are the ones that will haunt you the longest. So say it to them. Or say it to yourself in the mirror. Say it in a letter you'll never send or in a book millions might read someday. I think you deserve to look back on your life without a chorus of resounding voices saying **"I could've, but it's too late now"**.

There is a time for silence. There is a time waiting your turn. But if you know how you feel, and you clearly know what you need to say, you'll know it. **I don't think you should wait, I think you should speak now.**

Love, Taylor. ("Speak Now" Prologue)

PS: To all the boys who inspired this album, you should've known. 😉

![Image 2: Mine (Big Machine Records, 2010)](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=299x1024:format=png/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i3485f12110c797fe/version/1535848517/mine-big-machine-records-2010.png)

**The album's lead single "Mine" tells the story of a girl whose parents' failed marriage has caused her to take a pessimistic view on love. Over time, however, she falls in love with someone who convinces her to start believing in love again.**

Taylor was inspired to write "Mine" after reflecting on one of her unnamed crushes and explained that the song is about her tendency to run from love. The song contains elements of power-pop and its lyrics speak of the ups and downs of a young love.

"This is a situation where a guy that I just barely knew put his arm around me by the water, and I saw the entire relationship flash before my eyes, almost like a weird science-fiction movie. After I wrote the song, things sort of fell apart, as things so often do. And I hadn’t talked to him in a couple months. And the song came out, and that day, I got an e-mail from him. And I was like, ‘Yes!’ Because that one was sort of half-confession and half-prediction or projection of what I saw." -- Taylor Swift

The song was released as the lead single from "[Speak Now](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.jimdoweb.com/album-eras/speak-now/the-album/ "The Album")". Following an unauthorized internet leak, the song was released on August 4, 2010, two weeks earlier than the intended release date.

Critical reception for "Mine" was mostly positive. Taylor was praised for her ability to show a mature perspective on love, although some critics called the song "formulaic" for resonating her earlier works, notably "Love Story".

The song was commercially successful, as well; it became a top ten hit in Australia, Canada and Japan. In the United States, the song entered the Billboard Hot 100 at number three, making Taylor the second female artist in the history of the Hot 100 to debut multiple tracks in the top five during a calendar year after Mariah Carey did so in 1995.

The song's accompanying music video was directed by Roman White. It chronicles the romantic relationship between Taylor and her love interest played by British actor Toby Hemingway which ends with a marriage. The music video was met with great praise from contemporary critics who deemed it as "rather sweet," and "heartwarming." It received the coveted "Video of the Year Award" at the CMT Music Awards 2011.

![Image 3](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=102x10000:format=png/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i4e2ae67981e5173a/version/1548530989/image.png)

  

![Image 4: Sparks Fly (Big Machine Records, 2011)](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=299x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i2be1e055ba902073/version/1535849159/sparks-fly-big-machine-records-2011.jpg)

**"Sparks Fly" is a song Taylor wrote about falling for someone, despite knowing that she shouldn't -- but she can't deny the immediate connection.**

Taylor wrote the song when she was 16 years old, prior to the release of her debut single "[Tim McGraw](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.jimdoweb.com/album-eras/taylor-swift/the-songs/ "The Singles")" in 2006, after playing with her crush Jake Owen in a bar in Portland, Oregon. Following a 2007 live performance of the song, "Sparks Fly" grew in popularity among Taylor's fanbase. While "Speak Now" was under production, she received requests from fans to include the song on the album. As reported by _Taste of Country_, Taylor said:

"The song ‘Sparks Fly’ is about falling for someone that you maybe shouldn’t fall for, but you can‘t stop yourself because there’s such a connection, there’s such chemistry. This is a song that I wrote a few years ago and had been working on it ever since in the last two years and just honing in on little lyrics and changing them, so it’s really been awesome to see it change over the years." -- Taylor Swift

"Sparks Fly" received generally positive reviews by music critics, who praised it for its upbeat tempo. Others praised Taylor's lyrics of the song and have claimed that the song is a crossover between country and pop.

Following the release of "Speak Now", the song debuted at number 17 on the US Billboard Hot 100, due to strong digital sales. After the song was released as a single, it re-entered the US Billboard Hot 100 at #84. It peaked at number one at the US Billboard Hot Country Songs chart and was certified Platinum by the RIAA.

"Sparks Fly" was used as the opening song for the "[Speak Now World Tour](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.jimdoweb.com/album-eras/speak-now/speak-now-world-tour/ "Speak Now World Tour")". A music video for the song was released, featuring clips of various performances during the tour.

![Image 5](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=102x10000:format=png/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/ia6933865afda0cda/version/1548530996/image.png)

  

![Image 6: Back to December (Big Machine Records, 2010)](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=299x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i9a990233dc12b521/version/1535849607/back-to-december-big-machine-records-2010.jpg)

**"Back to December" is considered an orchestral country pop ballad and its lyrics are a remorseful plea for forgiveness for breaking up with a former lover.**

According to Taylor, "Back to December" is the first time she ever apologizes to someone in a song. She said "she never felt the need to apologize in a song before. But in the last two years I've experienced a lot, \[including\] a lot of different kinds of learning lessons. And sometimes you learn a lesson too late and at that point you need to apologize because you were careless." Critics speculate that the song is about Taylor Lautner, Taylor's ex-boyfriend. This was later confirmed by Lautner.

"‘Back To December’ is a song that addresses a first for me, in that I’ve never apologized to someone in a song before. This is about a person who was incredible to me -- just perfect in a relationship, and I was really careless with him. So, this is a song full of words that I would say to him that he deserves to hear." -- Taylor Swift

"Back to December" received positive reviews from critics, who regarded it as one of the highlights of "Speak Now". Critics have praised the song for its lyrics, melody, and vocals.

The song was the second single from the album and enjoyed commercial success, peaking at number six on the United States Billboard Hot 100, and at number seven in Canada. It also peaked at number three on the Billboard Hot Country Songs.

The song's accompanying music video, directed by Yoann Lemoine, laments the aftermath of a break-up between Taylor and her boyfriend.

![Image 7](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=102x10000:format=png/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/id518ceeb16849f5a/version/1548531006/image.png)

  

![Image 8](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=308x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i55d99724ec6e2ef0/version/1535911460/image.jpg)

**“Speak Now” transports listeners to Taylor’s daydream where she crashes her ex’s wedding so he won’t be stuck with a girl who doesn’t treat him right.**

Taylor wrote the song about interrupting a wedding, after conversing with her friend, whose ex-boyfriend would soon wed to someone else, and having a dream about one of her own ex-boyfriends marrying another girl.

"Speak Now" is rumored to be inspired by Hayley Williams of Paramore, who attended the wedding of her ex-boyfriend and ex-bandmate Josh Farro in April 2010.

"One of my friends, the guy she had been in love with since childhood was marrying this other girl. And my first inclination was to say, ‘Well, are you gonna speak now?’ And then I started thinking about what I would do if I was still in love with someone who was marrying someone who they shouldn’t be marrying. And so I wrote this song about exactly what my game plan would be." -- Taylor Swift

The song opened to critical acclaim for its lyrical detail. "Speak Now" had successful commercial outcomes in Canada and the United States, charting at number eight on both the Canadian Hot 100 and the Billboard Hot 100. Its appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 marked Taylor's sixth top ten debut, which made her the artist with the most top ten debuts in the history of the chart.

![Image 9](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=99x10000:format=png/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/ie59b49bd43b7fc04/version/1548531014/image.png)

  

![Image 10](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=284x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i8979fa12ccb92b12/version/1535912982/image.jpg)

**"Dear John” is an ode to Taylor’s short-lived relationship with fellow singer-songwriter John Mayer. The two notably collaborated on Mayer’s 2010 song “[Half of My Heart,](https://taylorswiftswitzerland.jimdoweb.com/album-eras/features/half-of-my-heart/ "Half of My Heart")” which was released four months before “Dear John”.**

Taylor conveys her feelings of frustration over the way she was treated by John and how she disregarded the warnings from others. Besides the obvious song title, there are multiple references to Mayer directly, including the mention of their almost ten-year age gap. Sonically, Taylor purposefully added guitar slurring to the background instrumentals, a guitar playing technique seen all throughout Mayer’s music.

"The song "Dear John" is sort of like the last email you would ever send to someone that you used to be in a relationship with. Usually people write this venting last email to someone and they say everything that they want to say to that person, and then they usually don't send it. I guess by putting this song on the album I am pushing send." -- Taylor Swift

Mayer, who is well-known for publicly talking about his relationships with various famous women in the press, has whined in an interview with _Rolling Stones_ about Taylor writing the song about him. In an issue of _Glamour_ magazine, Taylor called Mayer “presumptuous” for saying that he was “really humiliated” by the song’s lyrics. She went on to say that she did not want to hear his comments about the song, because of her desire to stay happy.

"I know it wasn’t good, so I don’t want to know. I put a high priority on staying happy, and I know what I can’t handle. It’s not that I’m this egomaniac and I don’t want to hear anything negative, because I do keep myself in check, but I’ve never developed that thick a skin. So I just kind of live a life, and I let all the gossip live somewhere else. If you go too far down the rabbit hole of what people think about you, it can change everything about who you are." -- Taylor Swift

Besides Mayer’s public statement to _Rolling Stone_ in 2012, he also replied to “Dear John” three years later, in his 2013 song “Paper Doll.” In the song, he directly replies to Taylor’s line, “You paint me a blue sky then go back and turn it to rain” with, “And if those angel wings don’t fly, someone’s going to paint you another sky.”

![Image 11: Mean (Big Machine Records,  2011)](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=299x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i775b970451b74121/version/1535913714/mean-big-machine-records-2011.jpg)

**"Mean" is an anti-bullying anthem Taylor wrote as a response to people who are critical of her.**

The song was solely written by Taylor and produced by Nathan Chapman with Taylor's aid. She revealed that the critic was someone who rebuked her performance with Stevie Nicks at the 52nd Grammy Awards. The critic was said to be Bob Lefsetz, who had given a captious review of her performance on his blog.

"There’s constructive criticism, there’s professional criticism, and then there’s just being mean. And there’s a line that you cross when you just start to attack everything about a person." -- Taylor Swift

"Mean" is heavy on fiddle and banjo and "the most country-sounding thing" Taylor has ever done according to Nathan Chapman.

The song garnered critical acclaim for its lyrical detail and country sound. "Mean" had successful commercial outcomes in the United States, charting at number eleven on the Billboard Hot 100and number two on the Hot Digital Songs Chart with 163,000 downloads.

_Rolling Stone_ ranked "Mean" at #24 on their list of the "100 Greatest Country Songs of All Time", the highest ranking for a song released in the 21st century.

In 2012, "Mean" won two GRAMMY Awards. One for "Best Country Solo Performance" and the other for "Best Country Song".

![Image 13: The Story of Us (Big Machine Records, 2011)](https://image.jimcdn.com/app/cms/image/transf/dimension=298x1024:format=jpg/path/s3628d4c0ebfcc161/image/i930a365cda475f45/version/1511037152/the-story-of-us-big-machine-records-2011.jpg)

**"The Story of Us" is about Taylor and her ex sitting next to each other at the 2010 CMT Awards, and refusing to speak to one another, despite the many things they had to say.**

The song was written by Taylor and produced by Nathan Chapman. In a 2010 interview with _USA Today_, Taylor explained:

"The Story of Us is about running into someone I had been in a relationship with at an awards show, and we were seated a few seats away from each other. I just wanted to say to him, “Is this killing you? Because it’s killing me. But I didn’t. But I couldn’t. Because we both had these silent shields up. I went home and I sat there at the kitchen table and I said to my mom, "I felt like I was standing alone in a crowded room.” Then I got up and ran into my bedroom, as she’s seen me do many times. And she probably assumed I had come up with a line in the song. And I had. And that was actually the last song I wrote on the album, and after I finished that one, I knew I was done." -- Taylor Swift

Based on the timeline given, it can be assumed that Taylor wrote this song sometime after July 19th, 2010, the day she wrote “Innocent,” which she thought would be the final song to be featured on the record.

"The Story of Us" was met with generally mixed reviews from critics, some of whom suggested that Swift is strongest when she lets her country roots shine.

Prior to its single release, the song debuted and peaked at number 41 on the Billboard Hot 100 and number 70 on the Canadian Hot 100 due to strong digital sales. It re-entered the Billboard Hot 100 at number 98 after its single release.

The music video of the song was directed by Noble Jones which took place in Vanderbilt University. It premiered on May 24, 2011 and was met with mostly positive reception among music critics for its departure from the usual high school setting of Taylor's previous videos. Taylor agreed that the video is different from the rest of her music videos. According to her, "the biggest difference between the new video and all the other ones is that I love to make a happy ending happen, and with this video, it doesn’t happen."
